connections.note: IEC is one of the few AAWSAP topics with a plausible conventional aerospace reading: a compact fusion device is what a small craft would need if it were producing the observed energy budget. The DIRD set contains four fusion-adjacent deliverables in total - Miley's IEC paper, Winterberg's advanced nuclear propulsion, Teofilo's aneutronic fusion propulsion for Lockheed Martin, and Culbreth's aneutronic fusion propulsion II.

desc: Plasma is the explanation that has to be defeated before any exotic reading is admissible, and it has held that role since the Condon Report, whose chapter by Martin D. Altschuler on 'Atmospheric Electricity and Plasma Interpretations of UFOs' worked through ball lightning, corona discharge and tornado-associated luminosity as candidate sources of sighting reports. The honest position is that plasma accounts for a real and probably substantial fraction of luminous-object reports, and that ball lightning itself remains incompletely explained - so the prosaic explanation invokes a phenomenon that is not fully understood either. What makes this a program domain rather than an atmospheric-science footnote is the dual use: the physics of generating, confining and steering plasma at a distance is the physics of directed-energy weapons and of radiofrequency plasma sheathing for radar signature control, work concentrated at the Air Force Research Laboratory's directed energy activity at Kirtland AFB - a base that recurs on this board for entirely separate reasons. An observer near such a test would see something that behaves like nothing they can name. Scoring high on this domain means an entity worked plasma physics in a defence or laboratory setting.
